clauses.reason: Discovery and the Skill-provided Worktrunk extend four existing owners.

updates.rationale: The user-level hook already identifies adopted repositories, so discovery needs no project file; failing open keeps a broken guard from stopping a session.
updates.statement: The guard is an optional PreToolUse Bash hook entry in a host's configuration that runs an installed Skill's scripts/command-guard, with a SessionStart entry running the same script in notice mode. It applies the whole rule set when the payload cwd lies in a Git work tree whose root holds signetum.toml and allows every command elsewhere. In such a repository the session entry prints one generic additional-context notice that development and delivery follow the Signetum Skill and names its SKILL.md; elsewhere it prints nothing. A missing interpreter, malformed payload, exception or timeout exits 0 with a diagnostic, and the sh entry maps every status other than 2 to 0. It prevents mistakes and is not a security boundary.

updates.rationale: The session entry is registered by the same command and replaced or removed with the guard, so the path both hooks name stays correct.
updates.statement: sh <skill>/scripts/signetum install places the Skill at each target: --host claude at ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/skills/signetum, --host codex at ${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}/skills/signetum, and --skills-dir DIR at DIR/signetum for any other tool. The source is the running Skill by default, a local Skill folder or release archive with --source, or a published release with --release <tag> or latest, verified like update. For each host target it writes one PreToolUse Bash entry and one SessionStart entry running that copy's scripts/command-guard into the host's user hook configuration, settings.json for Claude Code and hooks.json for Codex, preserving every other setting and replacing only Signetum guard entries. It is idempotent; --preview reports the exact plan and writes nothing; --remove deletes the Signetum guard entries and the placed Skill. It refuses a target folder that is not a Signetum Skill or lies inside a Git work tree and never edits a project. When a host target also has the signetum@signetum plugin installed at user scope, install removes it through that host's plugin manager after the Skill and hooks are in place, and reports a project-scope plugin with its removal command instead of running it.

updates.rationale: An earlier install registered only the PreToolUse entry; reporting the missing session entry lets the same command complete it.
updates.statement: When the running Skill sits in a Claude Code or Codex user skills directory and no hook entries in that host's user configuration or in the project's .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json or .codex/hooks.json run its scripts/command-guard for both PreToolUse and SessionStart, status reports one guard entry naming the host, the install command and the exact hook entries to add by hand. The guidance never blocks or changes an operation, and a Skill anywhere else reports nothing about the guard.

updates.rationale: A path-independent fingerprint lets every copy share one environment; including the Worktrunk pin re-prepares it when the pin changes.
updates.statement: The locked engine environment lives in ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/signetum/runtime/<fingerprint>, where the fingerprint covers the implementation digest, uv.lock, pyproject.toml and the pinned Worktrunk version and not the install path. A shared runtime/host-python link only starts the launcher, which verifies the environment for its own fingerprint. setup selects Python, uv and Worktrunk through Mise and records the Worktrunk executable and version beside the engine identity. setup and ordinary commands write nothing into the Skill directory except interpreter bytecode caches.

clauses.reason: The Skill owns its Worktrunk and reports stalled workspaces.

updates.rationale: Projects should not provision the Skill's own tool, and an internal identity name avoids any collision with older project declarations.
updates.statement: When the launcher supplies its Skill's pinned Worktrunk, the engine runs every Worktrunk operation with that absolute executable instead of resolving wt through the project's Mise configuration, and evidence binds its version output as the internal tool signetum-worktrunk, which a project cannot declare and member admission does not compare. Without the launcher, as in a development checkout, wt resolves through the project as before and no Worktrunk identity is bound. A project that still pins or declares Worktrunk, including as an ordinary validation tool, keeps working.

updates.rationale: Abandoned or forgotten work in parallel workspaces is otherwise found only when delivery stops; a derived read-only view needs no stored state.
updates.statement: Status derives, from local Git and workspace records without fetching, member workspaces that hold uncommitted changes while neither a commit nor the workspace opening is newer than a threshold, and member workspaces with no commit beyond their base for longer than a second threshold. The report is advisory, never blocks and starts nothing; the thresholds are status options with defaults of 30 and 60 minutes.

decisions.reason: A Skill that is rarely invoked and that needs every consumer to provision its own Worktrunk is not self-sufficient. Guard-owned discovery reuses the one registration install already performs and the adopted-repository test the guard already has, so no project file is touched; both hosts accept SessionStart hooks in the same configuration documents as PreToolUse. Provisioning Worktrunk beside Python and uv keeps one tool owner and one identity in evidence, and an internal identity name cannot collide with a project declaration, so existing projects keep working. A stalled-workspace report is a derived view of local workspace state and belongs with status, which already lists workspaces; leftovers lists checkouts created outside Signetum. Reopen if a host stops sending cwd in SessionStart payloads or Worktrunk can no longer be pinned through Mise.
